chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassha from Ahmad ibn A'iz from Abu Khadija from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The offspring of a Muslim man, when he dies, are given from the zakat and the fitra, just as their father was given, until they reach adulthood. So when they reach adulthood and recognize what their father recognized, they are given; and if they become Nasibi (Hostile Ones), they are not given.

key_terms.نَصَبُوا: Became Nasibi (Hostile Ones, specifically to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to receive zakat and fitra from the estate of a deceased Muslim man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the dependents of a deceased believer continue to receive zakat and fitra as long as they maintain the familial religious affiliation (wilayah), a principle rooted in the continuity of the father's spiritual status. It introduces a specific condition for cessation: if the children adopt the stance of the Nasibi (opponents of the Ahl al-Bayt), they are disqualified from receiving these funds, highlighting the political-theological dimension of zakat distribution in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the link between financial support and doctrinal fidelity within the community.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al washa, from Ahmad Bin Aiz, from Abu Khadeeja, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The offspring of the Muslim man, when he dies, would be given from the Zakāt and the Fitra, just as their father was given until they reach adulthood. So when they do reach adulthood and recognise (Al-Wilayah) what their father had recognised, they would be given, and if they turn to be Hostile Ones (Nasibis), they would not be given’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn ‘A’idh from abu Khadijah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Children of a Muslim man who dies can receive Zakat and al-Fitrah just as their father would receive, until they become adults and become knowledgeable of what their father was knowledgeable (believed in); they still can receive Zakat but if they become hostile, then Zakat is not given to them.”
